answer: A velvet-curtained hall admits one newcomer only after they stand and perform a sonnet they wrote themselves, judged live by three established poets who reject anything copied or machine-made; a rejected performance burns a 150 POA bond and bars re-entry for six epochs. The adjudicator wears a sable-trimmed robe, and each performance costs a $120 hall fee, so 100 fake identities need 100 original sonnets, $12,000 in fees and 15,000 POA in bonds.
